recipes.title: Runaway Lid
recipes.impossibleRule: The lid springs open whenever closing pressure is released.
recipes.goalRuleRelationship: Releasing the lid directly prevents keeping the container closed.
beats: {character} tries to close the lid, but it pops open against both palms. Eyes widen at the visible gap.
{character} pushes harder with both hands; the lid springs open and pins the forearms against the table.
{character} wedges the lid underneath an elbow; it pops open and lifts the elbow higher.
{character} changes to leaning sideways across the lid; it stays normal under broad body pressure.
{character} finally closes the lid and relaxes. It pops open again and scoops the character into the opening.
productionNotes: One character, one primary interaction, one stable location.
Broad movements; keep contact and the changing state visible.

recipes.title: Spoon Outgrows Breakfast
recipes.impossibleRule: Every lift makes the spoon grow larger.
recipes.goalRuleRelationship: Lifting a bite makes the eating tool too large to bring to the mouth.
beats: {character} tries to eat a snack, but the spoon is already huge beside the mouth. Eyes widen.
{character} lifts the spoon with both hands; it grows bigger and blocks the bowl.
{character} braces the spoon against the table and lifts from underneath; it grows larger across the table.
{character} changes to lifting with a shoulder; the spoon grows bigger and pins the character beside the bowl.
The giant spoon fills the frame. {character} is seated inside its scoop beside the tiny snack, unable to take a bite.

recipes.title: Brush Shrinks Away
recipes.impossibleRule: The brush becomes smaller whenever the character changes gripping strategy.
recipes.goalRuleRelationship: Every new way of holding the brush makes it less able to reach the hair.
beats: {character} tries to brush hair with a visibly tiny brush that barely reaches one curl. Eyes narrow at the size mismatch.
{character} switches to a broad palm grip; the brush shrinks and slips through the palm.
{character} braces it against the shoulder instead; it shrinks to the width of a single curl.
{character} brings the hair toward the brush rather than moving the brush; the final grip change shrinks it again.
The brush is now a single little bristle. {character} uses a broad curl to brush the brush, reversing who is grooming whom.
productionNotes: One character, one primary interaction, one stable location.

{character} pushes the handle with a forearm instead; the drawer reverses direction and opens toward the body.
{character} braces the open drawer with a shoulder and changes position sideways to reach inside.
{character} finally opens it and relaxes. The drawer slides back again, pulling the character into a broad crouch against the cabinet.

{character} pushes the chair closer with both hands; one step makes it slide back to its marked starting place.
{character} holds the chair underneath the body; shifting a foot makes it slide back and leaves the body crouched.
{character} changes to reaching backward while keeping both feet planted; the chair stays normal under the hands.
{character} finally sits and relaxes. One foot lifts and the chair slides back again, recreating the opening crouch.

recipes.title: Brush Will Not Let Go

recipes.goalRuleRelationship: The grooming stroke progressively fixes the tool in place instead of moving through the hair.

{character} pushes from underneath; the hair bends into a broad arch but the brush stays stuck.
{character} braces the handle against the shoulder and rolls sideways; the brush comes free while the curl springs away.
The released brush lands across the forehead and sticks there. {character} can no longer move the grooming tool at all.

{character} pushes sideways instead; the flexible wall bends underneath the ball and blocks the next reach.
{character} holds the wall steady with a shoulder and changes the pull direction upward; the ball finally releases.
